hook_text: For seventeen hundred years the world's population line was almost flat. Then it turned into a rocket.
clip_script: Year 1 AD: about three hundred million people on the whole planet. Fast forward seventeen centuries and it has barely doubled. Lots of babies were born, but lots of people died, from disease, famine and war. Then, around 1750, the line bends. More food. Clean water and sewers. Vaccines. Medicines. People stop dying young, but families still have many children. One billion around 1804. Two billion in 1927. Eight billion in 2022. Each new billion came faster than the last. Now there's a twist: families are having fewer children, so the curve is starting to bend again. Experts expect it to level off later this century, at around ten billion.
visual_style: A whiteboard line graph drawn left to right, flat for most of its length, then curving up sharply like a hockey stick; labels pop up at each billion; at the end the line begins to level off.
pacing: Flat, flat, flat, then a sudden rocket, then a gentle bend.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read the population graph.
